title: The Communist Manifesto
author: Karl Marx & Friedrich Engels
context: Commissioned by the Communist League and published in London in February 1848, this pamphlet was written during a period of massive political unrest across Europe. It explains the class struggle and critiques capitalism, serving as a call to action for the working class.
relatesToToday: Today, we see class struggle playing out in new ways. The traditional split between factory owners and factory workers now manifests as the divide between massive gig-economy tech platform owners (who control the apps and algorithms) and freelance gig workers (like rideshare drivers or delivery riders who sell their time without security or benefits). Similarly, rising global movements for unionization at massive logistics companies highlight the ongoing conflict over surplus value and workplace control.
keyTakeaways: History is driven by conflict between different classes in society.
Under capitalism, society is increasingly split into the Bourgeoisie (owners of factories/businesses) and the Proletariat (workers who sell their labor).
Capitalism creates its own destruction by expanding and uniting the working class, leading to a revolution.
